sections.heading: C — Managing space and speed
sections.markdown:
## C — Managing space and speed

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
Poor vehicle understanding, inattention and poor decisions can contribute to crashes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Manage six surrounding space areas and keep a cushion on every side of the vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
On dry pavement, a four-second following gap provides room to steer or brake around a highway hazard. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
Following too closely can leave no way to avoid a crash if the leading vehicle suddenly slows or stops. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A02
A safe following gap allows a response without a panic stop that could trigger a rear-end collision. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A02
Measure the gap by timing from the leading vehicle's rear bumper passing a fixed point until your vehicle reaches it; less than four seconds is too close. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A02
Increase the following gap on wet, slippery or unpaved roads because stopping takes longer. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A02
Leave a larger forward gap when a driver behind wants to pass, so that driver has room to return ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A02
Increase the gap behind a driver whose rearward view is blocked, because that driver may slow without seeing you. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A02
Leave extra room behind a large vehicle that blocks the view of the road ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A02
Increase the gap behind a heavily loaded vehicle or one towing a trailer. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A02
Allow extra following room when approaching slow vehicles, including bicycles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A02
Leave additional room behind school buses, taxis, other buses and hazardous-material trucks because they stop at rail crossings or unexpectedly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A02
Increase following space downhill, where slowing is harder, especially at high speed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A02
When stopped uphill, leave room for the vehicle ahead to roll backward as traffic starts. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A02
Side space provides an escape route if another vehicle abruptly enters your lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A02
Avoid traveling alongside other vehicles on multilane roads, where views and escape routes are blocked and blind spots are likely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A02
Keep as much separation as possible from oncoming vehicles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A02
Make room for highway entrants by signaling and moving to an inside lane only if safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A02
Leave space beside parked vehicles for opening doors, emerging people or vehicles pulling out. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A02
If neither side offers an escape path at least eight feet wide, increase the forward following gap. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A02
Normally drive near lane center; with parked cars on the right and oncoming traffic on the left, slow and choose a middle course. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A03
Help preserve rear space by holding a steady speed and signaling before slowing for a turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A03
If someone tailgates, move into the right lane when possible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A03
With no right lane, wait for a clear road ahead, then gently tap the brakes to reduce speed gradually and encourage a tailgater to pass. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A03
Look for a side escape route before slowing or stopping. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A03
Monitor rear-quarter traffic speed and distance, and turn your head to check those blind spots before changing lanes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A03
A blind spot is an area the driver cannot see without moving the head. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A03
Avoid lingering beside and slightly behind another vehicle; accelerate or fall back to leave its blind spot. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A03
When passing, clear the other driver's blind spot as quickly as safety permits. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A03
Look for problems 12 to 15 seconds ahead, about a city block or a quarter mile at highway speed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A03
Scan the whole road and its sides instead of staring only at the center. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A04
Scan ahead for slower entrants, stopped turning vehicles, hazard warnings and destination signs. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A04
Check the sides wherever traffic streams meet, including intersections, driveways and highway access points. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F35 | anchor: A04
At an intersection, look left, right and left again before pulling out because left-side traffic is closer and a later check may reveal missed traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F36 | anchor: A04
After entering an intersection, check both sides again rather than assuming other traffic will stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F37 | anchor: A04
If buildings, shrubs or parked vehicles block the cross-street view, edge forward slowly until the view clears. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F38 | anchor: A04
Check rear traffic frequently, especially before changing lanes or reversing. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F39 | anchor: A04
Entering a highway from a ramp or joining the road from a curb or shoulder counts as a lane change. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F40 | anchor: A04
Before a lane change, signal, check rear and side mirrors and make sure no vehicle is about to pass. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F41 | anchor: A04
Use quick shoulder checks as well as mirrors or sensors to check blind spots before moving lanes. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F42 | anchor: A04
A blind-spot check should not take the eyes off the road ahead for more than one second. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F43 | anchor: A04
On roads with three or more lanes, check every lane before changing because another driver may target the same gap. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F44 | anchor: A04
Before getting into the vehicle to reverse, inspect behind it for children or small objects. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F45 | anchor: A04
Before backing, turn to look through the rear window rather than depending only on mirrors or sensors. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F46 | anchor: A04
Choose speed using the posted limit, road condition, visibility and traffic flow because no speed is always safe. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F47 | anchor: A04
Communicate planned speed changes to other drivers. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F48 | anchor: A04
A posted maximum assumes ideal road, traffic and weather conditions. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F49 | anchor: A05
Pennsylvania's maximum posted speed limit is 70 mph. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F50 | anchor: A05
Interstate maximum-speed signs are posted after each interchange. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F51 | anchor: A05
On other highways, maximum-speed signs appear at approximately half-mile intervals. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F52 | anchor: A05
School-zone speed is limited to 15 mph while warning lights flash or during the signed times. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F53 | anchor: A05
Drive below the posted limit in wet, slippery, poorly visible or otherwise less-than-ideal conditions; a ticket is possible even below the limit. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F54 | anchor: A05
For economical driving, avoid rapid starts and hard braking. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F55 | anchor: A05
Avoiding the hottest part of the day can improve mileage because cooler, denser air can help power and efficiency. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F56 | anchor: A05
If the onboard-diagnostics lamp comes on, ask the dealer because fuel economy may be falling and emissions may be rising. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F57 | anchor: A05
Use an available ECO setting to smooth throttle inputs, optimize shifting and reduce air-conditioning load on the engine. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F58 | anchor: A05
Avoid unnecessary idling; when idling is needed, the handbook advises neutral or park to reduce engine load. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F59 | anchor: A05
Reduce driving through transit, cycling, walking, carpooling or combined errands to save travel costs and fuel. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F60 | anchor: A05
Night driving reduces vision and can expose the driver to headlight glare and more tired or impaired road users. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0043]

Misconceptions: posted limits assume ideal conditions; daytime running lamps do not replace required headlamps and taillamps; a turn signal does not grant priority.
Mnemonics: leave space, scan early, match conditions and communicate changes.
Glossary: hydroplaning means tires ride on water and lose road grip; a blind spot requires a head movement to inspect; overdriving headlights means stopping distance exceeds the illuminated view.
Dynamic facts: no officeholder, local answer or time-varying value is asserted; handbook edition currency is tracked as source debt in the authority part.

items.why: Forward, side and rear cushions require distinct gap and escape decisions.
Direct blind-spot checks and advance scanning require scenario practice.
Visibility conditions and dimming distances require applied recall.
Water, ice, snow and fog call for condition-specific decisions.
Signal distances and hand indications need maneuver-specific practice.
